prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring chosen proteins to ubiquitin ligases, and for identifying cereblon as the molecular target of thalidomide-type glue degraders

statement.case_for: I keep targeted protein degradation as my preferred single part. By my standard it is a game-changer: a new way for a small molecule to act, by inducing proximity between a target and a ubiquitin ligase and so changing what a molecule has to do to work, with consequences already visible in chemical biology, in many clinical-stage degraders and in approved cereblon-directed drugs. The round-1 exchange strengthened the mechanistic side of the case. Four of us arrived at the same trio independently, and Zou and Brzezinski both stress that ternary-complex co-crystal structures give an atomic, physical account of how a degrader works, which is the kind of evidence I trust. Handa's cereblon work turned a decades-old mystery into a molecular mechanism, and Crews and Deshaies supplied the design principle. I would write the citation so that it claims a general concept, not that any protein can be degraded, since degradability still depends on target-specific ternary-complex geometry and cooperativity.
statement.case_against: The reservations are real and I do not think the exchange removed them. No PROTAC is approved, so the heterobifunctional branch is validated by mechanism and clinical entry but not by a finished medicine; the approved imid drugs were found empirically and explained afterwards. The field can fairly be called pharmacology and chemical biology more than chemistry. Attribution is still a compromise: Sakamoto co-authored the first PROTAC paper with Crews and Deshaies, and Ciulli's VHL ligands made the design rational. A trio that pairs a PROTAC concept with a cereblon mechanism joins two lines of work, and I accept Chabes and Brzezinski that the citation must not suggest a single discovery. If the committee judges that waiting for a clinical verdict is wiser, I would accept that and move to B058, where the credit is clean and the maturity is beyond doubt.

responses.point: Heiner admires the single physical principle behind nanopore sensing and asks me for the best argument that its sequencing impact is more engineering than chemistry.
responses.response: The strongest form of that argument is about what the committee would be crediting. The threading principle is elegant and chemical in spirit, but the capability people actually use depends on engineered pore proteins, motor enzymes, signal processing and a commercial instrument, and the steps that made it work were spread across several groups. That is why your own concession matters: if Kasianowicz and Branton are left out of a Deamer, Akeson and Bayley trio, we need a rule for the cut that I cannot construct from priority alone. I do not call the work unworthy, and the sequencing impact is large; my point is only that its credit is less separable than the physics of the principle suggests. That is also the reason I keep B017 out of my alternatives, even though I take your ranking seriously.

responses.point: Emma asks why field-wide influence of Car-Parrinello is a stronger argument in 2026 than the lipid delivery case, given that the long delay suggests the committee has judged it differently before.
responses.response: I do not rest B058 on influence alone, and I accept that a long wait is not evidence of merit. My argument is that the conceptual step, treating electronic structure and nuclear dynamics together, made chemically reactive condensed-phase simulation possible and is now routine. The case also has the cleanest credit on the list. I also accept your own caveat that the decisive step in B019 is open between the Vancouver encapsulation chemistry and the lipid screening line. That is the reason B019 is now my second alternative and not my first: if the committee could settle that attribution, I would weigh your delivery case above B016. I still put B056 first because I judge its mechanism, its breadth of support and its priority record to be better established today than the lipid decisive-step question, not because medical impact counts less.

responses.point: Andrei separates the approved imid-type glue branch from the unapproved PROTAC branch, and asks whether one citation can hold PROTACs and glues together; he would fall back to B019 if B056 fails.
responses.response: I think the two can be held together as one idea, induced proximity to a ubiquitin ligase, but only if the citation names both strands openly, which is why I revised mine to say 'identifying cereblon as the molecular target' and not something broader. I agree with your point that the cereblon result is a mechanism, whereas the PROTAC concept is a design principle, and a trio spanning them is a judgement. I would rather be explicit about that than split into two parts, because two parts would need four or five names and would force us to drop Handa or Crews. Your B019 fallback is also close to my own revised alternative list, so I think we would not be far apart if B056 falters.

responses.point: Peter wants to know whether the case for Car-Parrinello rests on adoption or on the conceptual step of joining electronic structure and dynamics, and he keeps B058 as his alternative.
responses.response: It rests on the conceptual step; adoption is the confirmation, not the argument. I take your point that its reach into the daily practice of most chemists is narrower than that of C-N coupling, and I do not dismiss it. In this round I weigh B016 below B019 in my alternatives, not out of doubt about Buchwald and Hartwig, whose attribution is clean, but because the 2010 prize makes it look to several colleagues like an extension of known logic, and you concede that objection yourself. If the committee prefers a mature, tidy method prize over the degradation case, I would find B058 and B016 equally defensible, and I would not oppose either.

responses.point: Xiaodong moved from perovskites to B056 for mechanism, attribution and breadth, but notes that the cereblon structural basis must carry the glue half of the citation and that waiting may be wiser.
responses.response: The structural question you raise is the right one, and I think it is answered: the cereblon-ligand and ternary-complex structures show how imid-type molecules reshape the ligase surface, so the mechanism rests on determined structures. I do not need the glue half to be the whole of the case. On timing I take a different position than you, because the approved imid drugs already prove that the induced-proximity principle works in patients, and waiting for the first PROTAC approval would delay recognition of a concept whose validity is no longer in doubt. I would, however, keep the citation mechanistic and not clinical, so that it holds up whichever degrader is approved first.

uncertainties: Whether Handa or Ciulli should hold the third place, and whether Sakamoto's role in the first PROTAC paper makes a Crews, Deshaies and Handa trio vulnerable on priority.
Whether the committee will accept the absence of an approved PROTAC, given that the approved imid drugs validate the glue branch only.
Whether degradation will be accepted as chemistry and not as pharmacology and chemical biology.
Whether the lipid nanoparticle decisive step (Vancouver encapsulation chemistry versus lipidoid screening) can be settled, because that decides whether B019 should rank above B058 as a fallback.
statement.conflict_note: No change. I have no conflict or recusal need for any shortlisted candidate. My Warshel and EVB background, my Uppsala RNA and ribosome connections and my free-energy work do not link me to any credited name on B056, B058 or B019, and I have no tie to the other members that bears on these candidates beyond service on the committee with Brzezinski since 2015.
